blocker.summary: r456 fixed and verified r455's undefined-image regression: publish_write_address() now detects, via a delta on pinned_->edram_resolves() (the one signal PinnedShaderRuntime already exposes for 'did a resolve actually happen'), whether execute_frame() really touched the image -- it increments present_count() unconditionally even with no active EDRAM target, so success alone isn't proof. When no resolve occurred, falls back to a bare present_target_->clear() call directly (not via backend_->present_to_offscreen(), which would double-count the present in diagnostics()'s now-additive backend_+pinned_ sum, r455). Verified: native ctest 11/11, then a live probe with AC6_NATIVE_CAPTURE=1 against the real ISO: capture now succeeds (pixels=921600 = 1280x720, no more 'not in a blittable layout' error). non_black=0 distinct_colors=1 -- a uniform black image, exactly the old pre-r454 behavior, preserved without regression rather than a crash or an undefined image. Also characterized (not fixed) why real visual content still doesn't appear on this run: with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1 added, 9 fallbacks were logged with two distinct, already-documented-in-code rejection reasons -- the pinned registry's 271 oracle-derived shader variants (r255) simply don't cover every draw state this title uses, and rectangle-list expansion is only qualified for 16-bit guest indices (r265), not every format. Both are known coverage gaps, not new bugs. The r454-r456 wiring chain now has no known regression versus the old plain-clear baseline. Named for r457: (1) extend the pinned registry's coverage for the two characterized rejection reasons -- real, separate work, likely its own dedicated cycle; (2) once the wiring is judged mature enough, reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454/r455/r456). Still open, non-blocking: update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
